thread:
maria: quick check — bringing up cordelia-13b for GTN. did a tiny smoke run, some cost/quality numbers below. looking for ops + product guidance on routing and a minimal scorecard.
aj: paste the numbers?
maria: short summary: non-quant baseline (fp16) p50=110ms p95=420ms, tokens/request ~220, cost/request ~ $0.018. int8 reduced cost ~30% -> $0.012, p95 +30ms. int6 (experimental) reduced cost ~45% -> $0.01 but we saw a 3.8% drop on our QA-F1 slice.
kevin: what slices? long-form summarization or short QA?
maria: long-form extractive QA + multi-paragraph summarization were the worst. single-turn chat and short prompts preserved quality.
aj: do we have per-token cost assumptions? which infra?
maria: numbers on g4dn-like profile w/ batching 8. token compute cost normalized: fp16=0.000081/token, int8=0.000057/token, int6=0.000045/token. latency measured w/ continuous batching at avg inflight 12.
sam: can you share the small scorecard we ran? even a 3.8% drop might be fine if user-visible metrics unchanged.
maria: pasted sample scorecard: 
```
SCORECARD: cordelia-13b bringup (small-sample)
SLICES: short-chat, long-extract, code-qa
METRIC: QA-F1 | SUM-ROUGE-L | TOXICITY-REG
FP16: short 88.9 | long 79.2 | code 85.1
INT8: short 88.1 | long 77.9 | code 85.0
INT6: short 87.8 | long 75.4 | code 84.6
PASS-THRESH: drop <=2% on product-impt slices
OBS: long-extract int6 drop = 4.6% (fail), int8 drop = 1.6% (pass)
```
kevin: looks like int8 is the sweet spot for GTN routing. int6 probably needs more calibration or mixed-precision fallbacks.
maria: agreed. also saw some hallucination spikes on int6 for prompts > 900 tokens.
leo: from ops: can we do hybrid routing? e.g., detect long-extract -> route to fp16 or int8 fallback, else serve int6 for low-cost tasks.
aj: routing by slice is tricky at runtime. product would prefer a simple latency-based rule + retention of top-k answer QA confidence. maybe: if prompt tokens > 800 -> high-fidelity lane.
kevin: propose policy: default -> int8 cordelia, low-cost lane -> fallback to cheaper 7b-int4 for single-turn UI microtasks, high-fidelity lane -> fp16 cordelia when prompt>800 or QA confidence <0.7.
maria: quick econ snapshot per 100k requests: fp16 = $1,800 ; int8 = $1,200 ; int6 = $1,000 ; 7b-int4 = $420. (rough infra normalized).
sam: product question — what unit-econ gain by switching 30% traffic to 7b-int4?
maria: moving 30% -> 7b-int4 saves ~$360 per 100k requests vs all-int8, expected quality impact minimal if we only shift short-chat slice.
deploy-bot: deploy planned for canary 1710002000, models: cordelia-13b-int8, cordelia-13b-fp16 (fallback), cordelia-lite-7b-int4.
kevin: for GTN handoff add these pass criteria to the doc: 1) int8 long-slice drop <=2% vs fp16. 2) tail latency p95 int8 <= 500ms. 3) no hallucination spike >1.5x baseline on long prompts. 4) regression alerts wired to evals pipeline.
maria: will assemble a one-pager w/ minimal scorecard and routing flags. cc @aj @sam for product ok.
aj: product ok with hybrid rule if we can instrument per-route cost and QA-F1 in Console. canary looks good. :thumbsup:
kevin: one more ops note — warm KV cache matters for p50; recommend pre-warm for canary slices (run 200 synthetic long-extract queries before routing live traffic).
maria: thanks — i'll post the one-pager and create the canary ticket.
leo: ack, i'll add autoscaler levers for the fp16 pool and set a soft cap.
sam: thanks team. will prepare GTN blurb with the recommended economics and fallback playbook. :rocket:
